title.narrative: % of FP/SA client visits made by those living in severe multidimensional poverty at public sector sites supported by the project

description.narrative: MSI measures poverty using the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index created by the Oxford Poverty & Human Development Initiative (OPHI). We are unable to measure the nutrition indicator, so on advice from OPHI we instead double weight the child mortality indicator. We benchmark accordingly against the most recent Global MPI % severe poverty (at the time of writing, Global MPI 2020), using OPHIs syntax to limit to women of reproductive age (our client base) and double weighting child mortality in place of nutrition. The data is gathered during annual client exit interviews (CEIs).The results in the framework will be expressed with the confidence intervals and the target will be considered achieved if the upper bound of the CI is at the the national benchmark. Monitoring of this indicator under other donor funded programmes (e.g. WISH by FCDO) has demonstrated that this approach is good practice.

comment.narrative: Final targets are represented by DHS national benchmark of women of reproductive age living in severe multidimensional poverty target to achieve or maintain parity with these benchmarks

title.narrative: of occasions where asks presented by adolescent champions advocating for DRM are taken up by target stakeholders at subnational level

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of occasions where asks presented by adolescent champions advocating for domestic resource mobilisation are taken up by target stakeholders at subnational level in Y4H implementing countries. Uptake of an advocacy ask is defined as a policy draft, new policy, official strategy paper, change in legislation, budgetary commitments, implementation of commitments etc by decision makers, which can be only measured after some time. It is measured using project reports and internal Y4H M&E systems.

comment.narrative: Baseline survey to determine actual value
Foreseen in ExM presidential elections

In every country where a QIA was deployed a concrete support was provided to support a democratic cycle either through assistance to citizen observation groups support to CSO involved in promoting youth participation in elections or direct support to institutions and actors involved in the administration of the elections. Very often the QIA experts unveiled new possibilities and avenues for youth engagements that EU Delegations take up after the mission deployment but following up on the concrete suggestions of the QIA experts.Because the project intervened several times in the same countries 10 processes are relevant here compared to the 14 QIAs listed above. The countries where electoral processes were supported are the following Liberia Mozambique Madagascar Paraguay Mauritania Burundi Ethiopia Cote dIvoire So Tom and Prncipe and Ghana.
